resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) / Certificate of Compliance
resale_co.issued_by: Zoning Officer / Code Enforcement Officer (Zoning and Code Enforcement)
resale_co.lead_time: No application can be filed without a settlement date. All fees must be paid before scheduling an inspection.
resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the CCO application (needs a settlement date) and return it with payment (check or cash) to Zoning and Code Enforcement, 514 W. Atlantic Avenue, Haddon Heights. The applicant is responsible for scheduling all inspections and re-inspections after fees are paid.

evidence.quote: Per Ordinance 2018:1453, no residential properties may change ownership or tenancy until a Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) is issued by the Zoning Officer and a Smoke Detector/Carbon Monoxide Inspection is also required by the Fire Department.
As per Ordinance 2018:1453 it is required to apply for and receive a Certificate of Compliance issued by the Code Enforcement Officer
Please be aware that this inspection is DIFFERENT from the inspection the Fire Department conducts. You will need BOTH certificates in order to close.

resale_co.notes: Applies to change of ownership or tenancy of residential property. If an inspection fails, the property may close and/or be occupied without the certificate once the purchaser's agreement is accepted by the Enforcement Officer, for no more than 90 days while violations are abated (Sec. 262.2.1). The inspection checklist was not published online, so requirements are blank. Zoning Official and Code Enforcement Officer: Brian Kelly, zoning@haddonhts.com, 856-547-7164 ext. 33 (the form lists 856-546-2580). Current form is DocumentCenter/View/3128 (January 2025); an older 2021 copy (View/3121) has the same fees. Rental property registration and lead paint inspections are separate rental programs.

requirements: One smoke detector on each level including basement and any attic reachable by stairs; each level of each unit in a two-family
Ceiling-mounted at least 4 inches from walls, at least 36 inches from cold air returns and bathroom doors, away from ceiling fans; wall-mounted 4 to 12 inches below ceiling
UL-approved CO detector in the vicinity of each sleeping area
House number visible from the street, Arabic numerals at least 3 inches
2-A:10-B:C extinguisher no more than 10 lbs, charged, in a conspicuous place no more than 10 feet from the kitchen, instructions visible

authorities.name: Haddon Heights Fire Department, Bureau of Fire Prevention
authorities.lead_time: Lowest fee with 8 or more days advance notice; schedule early
authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Request for Inspection form and email it to one of the fire inspectors, fax it to 856-546-5340, or bring it to the office at 608 Station Avenue. Checks payable to Borough of Haddon Heights.

evidence.quote: SELLING YOUR HOME? The Bureau of Fire Prevention also handles the Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Compliance (CSDCMAC). This inspection is required prior to selling your home.
